body.statement: Using the branch-dual saddle handle in \(\text{def:full-class-handle}\), characterize \[\sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}}\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}\frac{\Gamma_D(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}.\] Is its value \(G\), so that the proportional schedule is already optimal, or can a nonproportional first-stage or survivor allocation achieve a strictly larger certified multiplier? Derive an attaining design and a matching saddle certificate in either case.
body.justification: The unrestricted two-batch design frontier is the genuine open content beyond the exact proportional-family theorem.
body.gap: Jun et al. and Jin et al. study batch constraints under different fixed-budget or fixed-confidence criteria; no cited theorem gives this heteroskedastic robust-gain saddle value.
body.consumer: A solution determines whether experimental platforms lose any worst-instance exponent by enforcing the simple proportional survivor-allocation interface.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching upper saddle bound, and hence the exact unrestricted robust multiplier and an attaining nonproportional-or-proportional design, remain open.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle specifies neither a compact closed feasible allocation set nor a dual minimax interchange theorem. The branchwise quadratic formula is explicit for each fixed design, but its infimum over all unique-best mean vectors is coupled across elimination branches, and no common dual witness presently bounds every nonproportional first-stage and survivor allocation by the proportional value.
obligation.attempted: Reduced every fixed design to unconditional Gaussian polyhedral programs and tested the proportional elimination and terminal witnesses. Those witnesses certify the proportional subclass but do not upper-bound arbitrary branch-specific survivor allocations; optimizing a witness separately after seeing each branch fails to produce one mean vector that is adversarial for the whole unrestricted design.
obligation.partial_result:
Because \(\mathfrak D_2\subseteq\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}\), the proved proportional design is feasible for the unrestricted problem, and therefore
\[
 \sup_{D\in\mathfrak D_2^{\mathrm{all}}}\inf_{\mu:\,|\arg\max_i\mu_i|=1}
 \frac{\Gamma_D(\mu)}{I_w(\mu)}\ge G.
\]
For every fixed two-batch design whose first-stage and branch-specific survivor fractions are specified, the unconditional Gaussian-polyhedron argument in \(\text{thm:finite-branch-exponent}\) also reduces its error exponent to a finite minimum of explicit convex quadratic programs.  What remains unresolved is the matching upper saddle bound after optimizing those programs jointly over all nonproportional allocations.
